IGUI_TraditionalPreservationSalt_Units: This spot has %1 of %2 diggings left.
IGUI_TraditionalPreservationSalt_InfoCha: The charge waiting comes out at %1 L of Brine in the bucket: %2
IGUI_TraditionalPreservationSalt_InfoBuc: The bucket holds %1 L of Brine: %2
IGUI_TraditionalPreservationSalt_InfoClo: Leaching goes by the clock, rain or shine.
IGUI_TraditionalPreservationSalt_FitSalt: The pan set over the hole and bedded in clay round its foot; the clay is lost when it comes off. It holds 30 L of brine and boils it down to a crust of salt: 1 Evaporated Salt for each litre of Brine. Top it up any time.
IGUI_TraditionalPreservationSalt_PanCrus: Salt Pan: dry, %1 Evaporated Salt to scrape
IGUI_TraditionalPreservationSalt_PanStat: Salt Pan: %1 / %2 L of brine, %3 C
IGUI_TraditionalPreservationSalt_PanNoBr: You have nothing with brine in it (Brine and water only).
IGUI_TraditionalPreservationSalt_PourInt: Room for %1 L. The salt stays in the pan as the water boils off.
IGUI_TraditionalPreservationSalt_ScrapeP: Scrapes out %1 Evaporated Salt. Part of a portion left over is lost.
IGUI_TraditionalPreservationSalt_PanHelp: Pour brine into the pan and light the fire: it comes to the boil in about half an hour and boils off 6 L an hour, leaving the salt.
Boiled dry: scrape the salt out with a knife. It waits, even on the fire.
The fire is out: the brine cools and waits. Add fuel and light it.
Banked: the embers keep the pan at the boil but boil it off a third as fast. Stoke the fire to boil it down.
